high.title: Foreign Investors Sell Nearly VND 5,000 Billion Worth of Vietnamese Stocks in Week April 20-24, Which Code Was the Focus of "Dumping"?
high.summary: Foreign investors continued significant net selling for the week April 20-24, totaling VND 4,816 billion across all exchanges. The VN-Index gained 36.12 points (+1.99%) to close at 1,853.29 points, conquering the 1,880 milestone before facing heavy selling pressure in the final session. Foreign net selling was concentrated on HoSE (VND 4,670 billion), HNX (VND 123 billion), and UPCoM (VND 23 billion). HPG led the buying side with VND 209 billion, followed by MSN (VND 169.8 billion) and MWG (VND 166.9 billion). On the selling side, FPT was the main focus of foreign dumping. This sustained foreign outflow pattern indicates continued portfolio rebalancing by international funds and creates downward pressure on Vietnamese equities. FX traders should monitor whether this capital outflow affects VND demand and potentially pressures the exchange rate.

high.title: Trade Deficit Reaches $7.9 Billion - What's Behind It?
high.summary: Vietnam recorded a trade deficit of $7.9 billion through April 15, with total trade value reaching $297.06 billion (+24.5% YoY). Exports hit $144.6 billion (+20.3%) while imports surged to $152.5 billion (+28.8%). The deficit reversed from previous surpluses, with $4.25 billion deficit in the first half of April alone. FDI enterprises dominated with $226 billion in trade value (+29.5% YoY), accounting for 76% of total trade and contributing 88% of growth. Domestic enterprises only reached $71.1 billion (24% share). Strong import growth was driven by machinery, equipment, and raw materials for production expansion. This widening trade deficit could pressure the current account and potentially affect VND stability. The SBV may need to monitor foreign reserve levels closely, and bond investors should watch for any policy responses to address the trade imbalance.

medium.title: TPBank AGM: Sets Profit Target of VND 10,300 Billion, Dividend Payment of 20% This Year
medium.summary: TPBank held its 2026 AGM with ambitious targets: pre-tax profit of VND 10,300 billion (+12% YoY), total assets of VND 600,000 billion (+19%), and customer deposits of VND 391,000 billion (+16%). The bank plans 20% dividend payment and aims to maintain NPL ratio below 2.5%. Strong profit growth targets from major banks indicate confidence in credit expansion and economic recovery.

medium.title: Vietnam's Largest Bank Wants to Use Over VND 13,000 Billion for Dividend Payment
medium.summary: BIDV will hold its AGM tomorrow with plans to increase total assets by 5-10% in 2026, maintain NPL below 1.6%, and potentially distribute over VND 13,000 billion in dividends. The bank's 2025 results showed total assets exceeding VND 3.26 million billion for the first time (+20.5% YoY). Large dividend distributions from major banks support domestic liquidity conditions and may influence deposit competition.

medium.title: HDBank AGM: Entering New Growth Cycle, 2026 Profit Plan Up Over 40%
medium.summary: HDBank conducted its AGM with both physical and virtual participation, targeting over 40% profit growth in 2026. The bank's aggressive expansion plans and technology investments at Galaxy Innovation Hub reflect confidence in the banking sector's growth prospects and digital transformation initiatives.

medium.title: Techcombank Plans "Massive" Dividend: 60% in Stock, 7% in Cash
medium.summary: Techcombank announced dividend plans of 7% cash dividend (VND 4,960 billion) plus 60% stock dividend, maintaining capital adequacy above 14% while continuing high growth. The combination of cash and stock dividends helps balance shareholder returns with capital retention for growth, reflecting strong banking sector profitability.
